Title: HTTP Client
Description: Send HTTP requests from your Windows machine through a local companion, with no account or MyDevTools proxy.
Seo_Title: HTTP Client for Windows — No Account or Cloud Proxy | MyDevTools
Keywords: HTTP client, REST client, API tester, Windows HTTP client, local API client, no account
PrivacyShort: Requests go directly from your Windows machine to the target
SetupIntro: Download and launch the Windows local companion required by this tool, then return to this page.
InstallAgent: About the Windows companion and download
SetupStep2: Launch MyDevTools Agent; its icon appears in the Windows system tray.
SetupStep3: Open the agent window from the tray icon and copy the displayed pairing code.
SetupStep4: Enter the code below. If the browser asks for local-network access, allow it for this connection.
LimitsNote: Requests accept up to 1 MiB bodies, responses up to 16 MiB, and timeouts up to 120 seconds.
PrivateSetupNote: Private, loopback and LAN targets are blocked by default. Restart the companion with --allow-private only when you intentionally need them. HTTP pairing grants only http.request; it never grants future scanner permissions.
PrivacyNote: The browser sends request details only to the companion on 127.0.0.1. The companion connects directly to the target; target URLs, headers and bodies can therefore leave your machine. MyDevTools servers do not receive or proxy them, and this page does not persist pairing codes, requests or responses.
PairCodeHint: Enter the fresh code from the companion window. It is cleared after every attempt.
HeadersHint: One Name: value header per line. Authorization is sent only when you enter it here.
BodyHint: Raw text or JSON, encoded as UTF-8. Set Content-Type explicitly when needed.
FollowRedirects: Follow redirects (up to 5; sensitive headers are removed across origins)
Disconnected: Disconnected and revoked the in-memory session.
PrivateAllowed: LAN access enabled at agent startup
BinaryPreview: Binary response. Use Download body to save the byte-exact content.
NoResponse: Connect and send a request to see its response.
PreviewTruncated: Preview limited to the first 1 MiB. The download contains the complete response.
ErrorHeaders: Each non-empty header line must use Name: value.
ErrorUrl: Enter a valid http:// or https:// URL.
ErrorBodyLimit: The request body exceeds the companion limit.
ErrorGeneric: The request could not be completed.
Error_agent_unavailable: The local companion is unavailable. Start it and allow local-network access in the browser.
Error_invalid_response: The companion returned an invalid response.
Error_invalid_request: The request contains an invalid method, URL, header or option.
Error_unauthorized: The session is missing or expired. Pair again.
Error_forbidden: This browser origin is not allowed by the companion.
Error_pairing_invalid: The pairing code is invalid. Use the latest code from the agent window.
Error_pairing_expired: The pairing code expired. Use the new code displayed in the agent window.
Error_pairing_rate_limited: Too many pairing attempts. Wait, then use the latest code.
Error_unsupported_capability: This companion does not support HTTP requests.
Error_private_network_denied: Private and LAN targets are disabled. Restart intentionally with --allow-private if needed.
Error_target_denied: The target is blocked by the companion security policy.
Error_response_too_large: The response exceeds the companion limit and was not truncated.
Error_request_too_large: The request exceeds the companion limit.
Error_busy: The companion is busy. Wait for another request to finish.
Error_network_error: The companion could not reach the target.
Error_incompatible_protocol: The companion protocol is incompatible. Install the current version.
Seo_Introduction: Send HTTP and HTTPS requests without creating an account or routing API credentials through a MyDevTools server. A small companion running on your Windows computer performs the network request and returns status, timing, headers and the response body to this page.
Seo_DetailedDescription: The browser pairs explicitly with the companion on `127.0.0.1` using a short-lived one-time code. The resulting session token stays in memory and grants only the `http.request` capability. Requests go from the companion directly to the target. Public targets are allowed by default; private, loopback and LAN addresses require the deliberate `--allow-private` startup option. Redirects are off by default and sensitive headers are removed when a redirect changes origin.
Seo_Examples: Use **GET** to inspect a JSON endpoint, **POST** with `Content-Type: application/json` to test an API payload, or **HEAD** to inspect response metadata without a body. Add `Authorization: Bearer …` only when the target API requires it; it is sent to that target, not to MyDevTools servers.
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Install and start the companion
Download the Windows x64 companion and launch it.

### Step 2: Pair explicitly
Request a code in the companion window, enter it here and click **Connect**. The code is cleared immediately after the attempt.

### Step 3: Compose the request
Choose a method, enter an HTTP or HTTPS URL, then add optional headers and a raw UTF-8 body.

### Step 4: Send and inspect
Send the request to view native status, timing, final URL, duplicate-preserving headers and a safe text preview. Download binary bodies byte-for-byte.
Seo_Tips:
- Keep redirects off when you need to inspect the first response.
- Credentials in an `Authorization` header go to the target service; avoid sharing screenshots that contain them.
- Leave private-network access disabled unless you deliberately test a trusted LAN service.
- Pairing this tool never authorizes future port or network scanning capabilities.
